predecessors.name: British Africa
predecessors.text: the Sudan of the 1899 UK-Egypt agreement, 'territories south of the 22nd parallel of latitude', administered under the 1902 boundary north of it to Halaib

ledger.x: 1956: Sudan becomes independent on 1 January.
1958: Egypt sends troops into the Halaib Triangle in February.
1958: the Egyptian troops withdraw the same month; Sudan keeps administering Halaib.
1969: the Democratic Republic of Sudan is proclaimed on 25 May.
1983: the second civil war begins in the south.
June 1983: the Bor and Pibor garrisons mutiny and the SPLA is founded.
1985: the Republic of Sudan is restored on 6 April.
1989 (bridge): the SPLA holds the south outside the government's towns.
July 1992: the government offensive.
1994: Egypt moves to take control of the Halaib Triangle.
1997: the SPLA takes Equatoria.
2000: Sudan withdraws its forces from Halaib in January, leaving Egypt in administrative control, which continues; Sudan still claims the Triangle (Bashir reasserted sovereignty in 2010).
2000: Halaib passes to Egyptian administration in January: Sudan withdrew its forces, leaving Egypt in administrative control; Egypt refuses arbitration, the claim stays open.
2005: peace in the south on 9 January.
9 January 2005: the Comprehensive Peace Agreement.
2011: Sudan seizes Abyei in May.
2011: South Sudan secedes on 9 July.
2012: South Sudan takes the Heglig oilfield on 10 April.
2012: South Sudan withdraws from Heglig.
2023: the RSF and the army go to war in Khartoum on 15 April.
2023: the RSF takes most of Darfur.
2023: the RSF takes Gezira State in December.
24-25 January 2024: Babanusa.
2024: the RSF besieges El Fasher from April.
20 June 2024: Al-Fulah.
29 June 2024: Singa.
23 November 2024: 'the SAF retook Singa following an offensive'; the page also has army counteroffensives in Sennar and Gezira in October 2024 that 'successfully recaptured' ground from the RSF.

wars.name: First Sudanese Civil War
wars.outcome: Ended by the Addis Ababa Agreement of March 1972, which gave regional autonomy to southern Sudan (infobox end 27 March 1972).

wars.name: Egyptian-Sudanese Halaib crisis
wars.outcome: Egyptian troops entered the Halaib Triangle and left in the same month; Sudan kept administering it.

wars.name: Second Sudanese Civil War
wars.outcome: Stalemate, then the Comprehensive Peace Agreement (9 January 2005): six years of autonomy for the south, a referendum and secession on 9 July 2011.

wars.name: War in Darfur
wars.outcome: Stalemate (infobox); peace agreements with rebel factions on 5 May 2006 (Darfur Peace Agreement), 14 July 2011 (Doha, with the LJM) and 31 August 2020 (Juba).

wars.name: Sudan-South Sudan conflict over Abyei and Heglig
wars.outcome: Sudan seized Abyei in May 2011; South Sudan held Heglig from 10 to about 20 April 2012 and withdrew; Sudanese victory (infobox); eight agreements signed in Addis Ababa on 27 September 2012.

wars.name: Sudanese civil war (2023-present)
